agentOutputs.headline: Selected mixed A and B sourcing reduces concentration versus all A baseline
agentOutputs.body: Selected plan preserves purchases from supplier A while increasing purchases from supplier B, creating a mixed sourcing allocation that lowers overall concentration versus the all A baseline. Inspect expected TCO impact {{delta_tco}} and the nearterm cash tail risk {{cash_outflow_p90}} when confirming the mix. Retained A purchase obligations and renewal exposure remain in the selected plan.

agentOutputs.headline: Selected mixed sourcing reduces concentration versus all A
agentOutputs.body: Selected allocation retains supplier A and adds supplier B as a meaningful secondary source. This mixed sourcing reduces overall concentration compared with the all A baseline while maintaining active purchases from A and associated renewal exposure. Delivery risk metrics indicate low stockout probability for the selected mix {{stockout_probability}}. Alternative paths include keeping all supply with A or exiting A to B only; those remain conditional and are listed as options.

agentOutputs.headline: Mixed sourcing reduces supplier A dependence relative to baseline
agentOutputs.body: Selected action keeps both suppliers in the plan with a majority share remaining with supplier A and a significant share from supplier B. This reduces dependence on supplier A relative to the all-A baseline while supply concentration remains lower than baseline. Maintain the minimum purchase exposure to supplier A under the renewal terms. Inspect current cash tail risk {{cash_outflow_p90}} and the computed stockout probability {{stockout_probability}} for this mixed allocation before committing.

criticIssues.headline: Omitted compound risk involving locked forecast terms and holding cost changes
criticIssues.body: The analysis does not explicitly address the interaction between locked forecast terms and holding cost changes under the selected mixed sourcing allocation. Although the roles acknowledge the retention of supplier A and the active minimum purchase commitments under renewal, they fail to specify that holding costs shift relative to the baseline and that excess units could become a compounded financial strain if demand were to decrease significantly, as the committed minimums are locked at renewal.

brief.recommendation: Retain the mixed A and B allocation as selected, keeping supplier A and adding supplier B to lower concentration while honoring the locked minimum purchases from A.
brief.rationale: The chosen mix preserves required minimum obligations to supplier A at renewal while introducing meaningful supply from supplier B to reduce dependence on A versus the all A baseline. This selection does not terminate supplier A, does not trigger an exit fee, and does not move to B-only sourcing. It balances service and cash tradeoffs qualitatively by improving delivery reliability under the mixed allocation and keeping projected cash tail risk within the enforced ceiling.
brief.formula: TCO = purchase + holding + stockout loss + renewal premium + termination fee
formulaNotes: All costs and risk measures originate from this verified simulation; cash tail risk is separate from expected total cost.
brief.guardrail: All displayed claims passed field-bound numeric and evidence validation.
